extracted.intended_audience: attorneys filing or defending Federal Circuit appeals from PTAB decisions (IPR/PGR practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step procedural and drafting guidance for taking appeals from PTAB final written decisions to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, including deadlines, filing mechanics, brief contents/formatting, appendix preparation, motions, and post-judgment steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Appeal is due 63 days after the final written decision OR action on the first timely rehearing request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has discretion to extend the deadline on a timely written request to the Solicitor, but the request does not toll the deadline. Authorities cited: 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(a)(1); 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(b)(1); 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(c)(1); Fed. Cir. R. 15(a)(1); FRAP 4(a)(3). File the notice at the PTAB via PTAB E2E and in paper with the USPTO Director, and upload a combined PDF to the Federal Circuit CM/ECF NextGen (pay $500 fee). Include certificate of filing showing Director and Federal Circuit filing and certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Cross-Appeal timing and threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of cross-appeal is due the later of (a) 14 days after the other party’s notice of appeal; or (b) the original notice of appeal deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File cross-appeal only if you seek to enlarge the PTAB’s decision. Changing an outcome on a claim enlarges the decision; changing outcome on a ground/argument does not unless it would change claim outcome. General rule: file a cross-appeal if you 'completely lose' on at least one claim. Arguments rejected or ignored can be advanced as alternative reasons to affirm or to seek remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of Appearance, Certificate of Interest, and Docketing Statement deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: These documents are due 14 days after the appeal is docketed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also file a FRAP 44(a) letter if your appeal raises a constitutional issue. Authority: Fed. Cir. R. 15(a)(1); docketing tasks done via CM/ECF Forms and Certificates submenu. Name PDFs carefully because file names show up in ECF notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Appendix Designations deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial appendix designations (served but not filed) are due 14 days after the Certified List is served; appellee’s additional designations are due 14 days later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: FRAP 30(b)(1). The certified list service kicks off the remaining deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant Principal Brief (opening) deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant’s principal brief (Opening/Blue Brief) is due 60 days after the USPTO serves the Certified List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. Cir. R. 31(a)(1)(B). Word-count limits and brief contents (see separate criteria). In cross-appeal situations, deadlines and brief types adjust per Fed. Cir. Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellee Principal Brief (response) deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellee’s principal brief (Red Brief) is due 40 days after Appellant’s Principal Brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. Cir. R. 31(a)(2). In a cross-appeal the same deadline applies to the Appellee/Cross-Appellant’s principal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant Reply brief and combined response/reply deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant’s Reply (Gray Brief) is due 21 days after Appellee’s Principal Brief; in a cross-appeal the Appellant’s combined response & reply deadline is 40 days after Appellee/Cross-Appellant’s principal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-appellant’s reply is due 21 days after Appellant’s combined response and reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Appendix deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Final appendix is due 7 days after the last reply brief is served and filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Settlement Discussion Statement must be filed no later than the filing of the joint appendix. Paper copies of briefs & appendix may be requested by the Court and are due within five business days of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement discussion timing and statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must discuss settlement within 7 days of the last principal brief (or of the appellant’s combined reply/response in cross-appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion must be live (in person or by phone). By the time the appendix is due, the parties must file either a joint statement of compliance indicating settlement discussions occurred (cover page sufficient) or a joint motion to dismiss under FRAP 42(b). File the joint statement via CM/ECF Forms and Certificates submenu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper copies timing and quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Court requests paper copies, they are due within five business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the appellant: 6 copies of its principal brief and reply brief (or reply and response in a cross-appeal) and 6 copies of the joint appendix. From the appellee: 6 copies of its principal brief (and its reply brief in a cross-appeal). Only the paper copies need the colored covers specified by the court. Double-sided printing strongly recommended. Find a vendor early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument conflict notice standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Form 32 to advise of scheduling conflicts for oral argument; only conflicts of the arguing attorney matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each conflicted date, the attorney must provide a statement establishing good cause. Good examples: major life events, on-calendar oral argument or trial before another tribunal. Bad examples: not-yet-booked vacation, client unavailability, strategic delay. If no conflicts, indicate 'none' via CM/ECF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument response form and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Once Court issues an oral argument notice, arguing counsel should use Form 33 to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the pandemic Forms 33A-33C relate to COVID-19 precautions. The Court is lenient about argument/rebuttal time split in the author’s experience. Respond via CM/ECF Calendar submenu, upload PDF, select party, and submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions required components
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion must include: Cover Page; Certificate of Interest (Form 9 or equivalent); Statement of Consent (whether opposed/consent); Argument (grounds, relief sought, supporting legal argument); Conclusion; Certificate of Compliance (Form 19 or equivalent); Affidavit (if necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word-count limits: Motion/response 5,200 words; Reply 2,600 words. A response is due 10 days after a motion; a reply is due 7 days after the response. File motions via CM/ECF Motions submenu indicating consented/opposed status and relief requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to extend specific requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to extend should be filed at least 7 days before the deadline to be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed closer than 7 days, an affidavit establishing extraordinary circumstances (e.g., natural disaster) is required. The motion must state: the date to be extended; the revised date sought; the number of days requested; and the total number of days of extension previously granted to the movant across ALL deadlines. A motion to extend by more than 14 days also requires an affidavit establishing 'good cause.' Court rarely denies extensions, but parties should not expect further extensions after a full 60-day extension on an opening brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing responses and replies to motions in CM/ECF
rubrics_metrics.description: To file a response/opposition or reply to a motion, use the Response/Opposition or Reply events from the Response/Reply submenu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify by ECF number the filing you respond to, select your party, upload the PDF, review docket text, and submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and content rules for bills of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking costs is limited to the lesser of its actual costs or the maximum allowable cost; use Form 24 and instructions to prepare a bill of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flatten the bill and prepare a combined PDF with vendor invoices to support costs claimed. The Court prefers stipulation on costs; objections are limited to 5 pages. File the bill via CM/ECF Forms and Certificates submenu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate effects and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After rehearing time expires or after denial of rehearing, the Federal Circuit issues the mandate which ends the appeal and implements the judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remand is ordered the case returns to the PTAB; otherwise PTAB issues trial certificate. If a prevailing party filed a bill of costs, the mandate will tax costs per that bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission and CM/ECF NextGen account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit uses CM/ECF NextGen for electronic filings and CM/ECF accounts are limited to admitted attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register as an attorney filer at pacer.uscourts.gov/register-account/attorney-filers-cmecf to move for admission. Admission by written motion requires notarization and at least one of: sponsorship by an already admitted attorney; or a certificate of good standing from another federal court or a final state court. USPTO 'sponsored' paralegals cannot be given CM/ECF accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal contents guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the notice of appeal on your PTAB paper and succinctly list the issues you intend to appeal, including a catch-all statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example catch-all: 'the Board’s consideration of the expert testimony, prior art, and other evidence in the record; the Board’s factual findings, conclusions of law, or other determinations... as well as all other issues decided adversely to [CLIENT]...' Include a certificate of filing indicating filing with (1) USPTO Director and (2) Federal Circuit, and the usual certificate of service on opposing counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal filing mechanics at the PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: File a notice of appeal at the PTAB through PTAB E2E and follow the AIA Review Appeal 'Paper' -> 'Notice of Appeal' workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate party and review for successful filing. Use 'My Docket' -> 'AIA Review Actions' -> 'File an Appeal' and upload the PDF. Confirm successful filing. (Slides reproduce PTAB E2E guide steps.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal filing mechanics at the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Log into Federal Circuit CM/ECF and select 'Agency Petition/NOA (Fee)' to upload the combined PDF and pay the $500 notice of appeal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CM/ECF screens to pay and submit; you will receive an email receipt for the filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified List function and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The certified list is a list of papers filed during the PTAB proceeding and is filed with the Federal Circuit by a PTAB paralegal within 40 days of the notice of docketing (usually Day 38 or 39).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will receive the certified list by email; service of the certified list triggers all remaining deadlines in a Federal Circuit appeal of a PTAB proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial appendix organization order
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial appendix designations should place documents in this numbered order: (1) Final written decision; (2) Certified List; (3) All other PTAB papers in numerical order; (4) Exhibits in numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize a file folder and start file names with the item number and leading zeroes (e.g., '001 Final Written Decision') for ease of organization. Prepare a combined PDF of the documents in that order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix pagination and footer conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an 'Appx' footer with page numbering on the appendix PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Adobe Acrobat Add Header and Footer tool; type 'Appx' in Center Footer Text, then insert page number. Recommended footer font 14-pt Arial. Use 'Shrink document to avoid overwriting text and graphics.' For appendix citations: To a single page: Appx500; to a pincite within a single page: Appx500(¶ 33) OR Appx500(13:15-22) — No space after 'Appx'. For a page range: Appx500-503 (always include all leading digits; no 'Appx' next to end page). Pincite within page range: Appx500-503(¶¶ 33-42) or Appx500-503(13:15-16:22). Use semicolons to separate citations in a list. Choose whether to enclose citations in parentheses but be consistent. Periods/punctuation go outside the pincite parentheses but inside any parentheses enclosing an entire citation (e.g., (Appx500(¶ 33).)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing appendix designation letter and tooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Export CSV paper and exhibit lists from PTAB E2E, populate a paginator spreadsheet, check pagination against combined PDF, and copy select columns into a four-column table for the letter to appellee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 'Magic Appendix Paginator' spreadsheet (author's tool) to assemble items and verify pagination. Hold on to the spreadsheet for preparing the final appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final appendix inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The final appendix must include the full final written decision, certified list, and all cited patents and pre-grant publications in their entireties; recommended to include the entire notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all other documents, include (1) the document’s first page; (2) all cited pages; and (3) any pages adjacent to cited pages needed for context. Delete any row/item with no pages cited. Compile a list of every appendix citation from both parties’ briefs to assemble the final appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final appendix volume-splitting and binding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the final appendix into multiple volumes if printing single-sided and there are more than 400 pages (including TOC), or double-sided and more than 800 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volumes need not be evenly split. Best practices: consider placing papers in one volume and exhibits in another; don’t split a single document over multiple volumes; don’t use an unnecessary number of volumes. Each volume must have a cover page and full table of contents; if multiple volumes, include volume number and page range at top and list items’ entire page ranges by volume. List both parties’ counsel at bottom.

rubrics_metrics.name: General formatting rules for briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended fonts and spacing: 14-pt Times New Roman or Century Schoolbook; body text double-spaced; block quotes indented and may be single-spaced (author usually 1"-indent, 1.5 spacing); footnotes may be single-spaced (author usually double-space for legibility); page numbers 14-pt centered bottom same font as body text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow consistent spacing and indentation rules for readability. Flatten PDFs before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix citation formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific required appendix citation formats for pincites, page ranges, and lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To a single page: Appx500. Pincite within single page: Appx500(¶ 33) OR Appx500(13:15-22) — no space after 'Appx'. Page range: Appx500-503 (include all leading digits). Pincite in page range: Appx500-503(¶¶ 33-42) or Appx500-503(13:15-16:22). Use semicolons to separate list citations. Punctuation rules: periods go outside pincite parentheses but inside any parentheses enclosing the entire citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal brief required components and order
rubrics_metrics.description: A principal brief must include the following components in order: Cover Page; Certificate of Interest (Form 9 or equivalent); Table of Contents; Table of Authorities; Statement of Related Cases (prose version of Certificate of Interest); Introduction (optional but recommended); Jurisdictional Statement (appellee: areas of disagreement only); Statement of the Issues (appellee: areas of disagreement only); Statement of the Case (appellee: areas of disagreement only); Summary of the Argument (one numbered subsection per issue); Statement of Standard of Review (appellee: areas of disagreement only); Argument (one top-level heading per issue); Conclusion and Statement of Relief Sought; Addendum (appellant must include final written decision and copy of the patent with appendix pagination; optional cover sheet listing addendum items recommended); Certificate of Compliance (Form 19 or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the order strictly and include required addendum items for appellants. Flatten PDFs before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief required components and order
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief must include, in order: Cover Page; Certificate of Interest (Form 9 or equivalent); Table of Contents; Table of Authorities; Argument; Conclusion and Statement of Relief Sought; Certificate of Compliance (Form 19 or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to required components and order; observe word-count limits for replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief cover page content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside cover must include case number (top center), court name, official caption (must exactly match PACER/docketing notice), nature of proceeding and tribunal appealed from (including PTAB judges’ names now encouraged), title of the brief, and counsel contact info (name, address, telephone; other contact info optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inside cover should include contact information for other counsel if it doesn’t fit on the outside cover and the language of a claim at issue (or on a page immediately after the cover if space requires). Ensure the caption exactly matches the official caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of compliance placement and word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Place Form 19 or equivalent at the end of the brief and indicate word count; select the typeface box if used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal briefs: 14,000 words; Reply: 7,000 words. See Fed. Cir. R. 28.1 for cross-appeal word counts. Sections that do NOT count toward word limits: cover page & inside cover; certificate of interest; tables of contents & authorities; statement of related cases; signature block; addendum; certificate of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing briefs in CM/ECF event selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Brief/Appendix or Joinder' event from the 'Briefs' submenu when filing briefs and appendix; don’t use 'Opposition' or 'Reply' events which are for motions responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the screens select your party and the type of brief: Opening Brief; Response Brief; Reply Brief. Select email service, upload the PDF, review docket text, and submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement discussion filings via CM/ECF
rubrics_metrics.description: File the joint statement of compliance or joint motion to dismiss using the 'Joint Statement of Compliance – FCR 33' form from the Forms and Certificates submenu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select your party, upload PDF, review docket text, and submit. A joint statement should include a cover page but need not include much else.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forms and flattening PDFs before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Federal Circuit forms where directed (Form 8A for Entry of Appearance, Form 9 Certificate of Interest, Form 26 Docketing Statement, Form 19 Certificate of Compliance, Form 24 Bill of Costs, Form 32/33 for oral argument responses, etc.) and flatten PDFs before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry of Appearance: list every represented party by full legal name (no 'et al.'). Certificate of Interest: list same Real Parties in Interest as at PTAB, list legal representatives who appeared at PTAB or will appear at Federal Circuit, list related cases including concurrent district court litigation. Docketing Statement: use Form 26, check 'Final Judgment' box for appeal of a final written decision, list multiple related appeals as appropriate. Save Word equivalents if helpful for inclusion in briefs.
